# Troubleshooting and FAQ

Every entry below was met while building or testing TTpipe, and each is
written as **symptom, cause, fix**. Where a statement rests on general
Snakemake, conda or SLURM behaviour rather than on something checked in this
repository, it carries a note saying "general knowledge". For the short list
of messages that TTpipe itself prints when it checks your samplesheet and
config (missing column, unknown condition, and so on), see the table in the
[README](https://github.com/jpflores-13/TTpipe#troubleshooting). Where to look
for logs: per-sample logs are in `<outputDir>/<sample>/logs/`, the others in
`<outputDir>/logs/`, SLURM job logs in `<outputDir>/logs_slurm/`.

## `Disk quota exceeded` while building environments or starting Snakemake

**Symptom.** The first run stops while conda builds an environment, or
Snakemake fails to start, with `Disk quota exceeded`.

**Cause.** Two caches sit in your home directory by default. Conda keeps
downloaded packages in a `pkgs` folder under the Miniforge directory, which
is usually in `$HOME` (`$HOME/miniforge3`), and Snakemake writes
`~/.cache/snakemake`. Clusters often give home directories a small quota.
Seen on the first real run of TTpipe.

**Fix.** Point the caches at a location with space (a scratch or project
folder; use your own path) before launching, and free the space already used:

```bash
export CONDA_PKGS_DIRS=/path/with/space/conda_pkgs
export XDG_CACHE_HOME=/path/with/space/cache
export TMPDIR=/path/with/space/tmp
mkdir -p "$CONDA_PKGS_DIRS" "$XDG_CACHE_HOME" "$TMPDIR"
conda clean --packages        # removes the cached packages in the old location
```

Put the `export` lines in `~/.bashrc` so that every shell, including the one
that runs `sbatch`, has them. The conda environments themselves go into
`.snakemake/conda` in the folder you launch from, so launch from a folder
with enough space too. (`TMPDIR` is read by many tools; that it also moves
conda's temporary files is general knowledge.)

## MultiQC fails with `No module named 'pkg_resources'`

**Symptom.** The `multiqc` rule fails at import with
`No module named 'pkg_resources'`.

**Cause.** MultiQC 1.14, the version TTpipe pins, imports `pkg_resources`,
which setuptools 70 and later no longer provide. Older checkouts of TTpipe did
not pin setuptools.

**Fix.** Update to a checkout in which `envs/ttpipe_multiqc.yml` contains
`setuptools<70`. Because the environment file changed, Snakemake rebuilds that
environment on the next run; just resubmit. To skip MultiQC altogether, set
`multiqc: false` in the config.

## DESeq2 fails with `sample names differ between the count matrix and the sample table`

**Symptom.** The `deseq2` rule stops with that message after you added
samples to a folder that already had results.

**Cause.** In older versions, the sample table `counts/samples_deseq2.txt`
was not tied to the samplesheet, so Snakemake kept the table from the earlier,
smaller run while the count matrix had the new samples.

**Fix.** Fixed: the samplesheet is now an input of the `sample_table` rule
(`workflows/TTpipe.snakefile`), so editing it regenerates the table. If the
message ever recurs, delete `<outputDir>/counts/samples_deseq2.txt` and run
again. The same message also appears, for a different reason, in an
analysis-only run whose count-matrix column names do not match the samplesheet
`Name` values; then rename the columns or the names.

## Editing a comment in `envs/*.yml` reruns jobs

**Symptom.** After you change anything in a file in `envs/`, even a comment,
Snakemake wants to rerun every rule that uses that environment, including
long alignment jobs.

**Cause.** Snakemake treats a changed environment definition as a reason to
rerun (general knowledge about Snakemake 8's rerun triggers; it is not
specific to TTpipe).

**Fix.** Ask Snakemake to ignore that trigger. The launcher passes extra
arguments through, so:

```bash
bash TTpipe.sh -n --rerun-triggers mtime params input code     # check the plan first
sbatch TTpipe.sh --rerun-triggers mtime params input code
```

The list omits `software-env`, the trigger for environment changes. Use this
only when you know the change does not alter the software.

## Chromosome names differ between the GTF and the genome

**Symptom.** The workflow stops at startup with: `chromosome names differ
between the GTF (first sequence '1') and the genome (first sequence 'chr1')`
(the names in your message will be your own).

**Cause.** One file uses `1`, `2`, `X` (Ensembl style) and the other `chr1`,
`chr2`, `chrX` (GENCODE and UCSC style). The check is in
`workflows/rules/common.smk`. It compares only the naming style of the first
sequence, so it cannot catch every mismatch (for example different contig
sets).

**Fix.** Use a FASTA (or STAR index) and a GTF from the same source, for
example both from GENCODE. See [Setup](setup.qmd#the-chromosome-name-trap).

## All counts are zero, or very small

**Symptom.** `counts/counts_deseq2.txt` is all zeros or has tiny counts;
DESeq2 reports almost nothing.

**Cause.** The most common one is a GTF without `gene` lines, or one where
the gene id is not in a `gene_id` attribute. TTpipe counts with HTSeq using
`htseq_feature: 'gene'` and `htseq_id_attribute: 'gene_id'`, and the gene
table is built from the `gene` lines. If the keys do not match your GTF,
nothing is counted. A chromosome-name mismatch (previous entry) that the
startup check did not catch gives the same picture.

**Fix.** Look at your GTF: `awk '$3=="gene"' your.gtf | head -2` should show
lines whose last column contains `gene_id "..."`. If your annotation has no
such lines, or names the id differently, set `htseq_feature` and
`htseq_id_attribute` accordingly, but read the caveat in
[Setup](setup.qmd#other-genomes) first: counting exons instead of genes
changes the science. Also compare chromosome names between the GTF and the
FASTA, and check that `strandedness` is right (the QC report's strandedness
panel shows it).

## STAR runs out of memory or the job is killed

**Symptom.** `star_align` or `star_index` ends with `OUT_OF_MEMORY` (in
`sacct`) or a "killed" message in its log.

**Cause.** The per-rule memory in the profile is a starting value. On a
mouse genome STAR alignment measured about 26 GB and the index build about
29 GB; larger genomes need more and have not been measured.

**Fix.** Raise `mem_mb` for `star_align` and `star_index` in your profile's
`config.yaml` (`set-resources:`), keeping a margin, and resubmit. Finished
jobs are kept. Check actual use with `seff <jobid>` or `sacct` (see
[Cluster reference](cluster.qmd#tuning-resources)). On `profiles/local` the
global `mem_mb=64000` limit also decides how many jobs run at once; lower or
raise it to match your machine.

## SLURM rejects the submission and mentions the account

**Symptom.** Jobs are not submitted; SLURM reports an invalid account or
association.

**Cause.** The profile still contains the `<your-slurm-account>` or
`<account>` placeholder (the `longleaf` and `pioneer` profiles and
`slurm-template` ship with one).

**Fix.** Find your account with `sacctmgr show assoc user=$USER` and write it
into `slurm_account:` in the profile's `config.yaml`; delete the line if your
cluster does not use accounts. `profiles/slurm-template/config.yaml` explains
the same. Also check `slurm_partition` against `sinfo -s`.

## "The workflow is locked" after an interrupted run

**Symptom.** Snakemake refuses to start and says the directory is locked.

**Cause.** A previous run was killed (for example by the launcher's wall-time
limit) before Snakemake could release its lock.

**Fix.** Make sure no TTpipe launcher is still running (`squeue -u $USER`),
then:

```bash
bash unlock.sh
sbatch TTpipe.sh
```

`unlock.sh` accepts `--configfile` and `--profile` like the launcher.

## The cluster's compute nodes have no internet access

**Symptom.** Environment builds fail with network or download errors inside a
job.

**Cause.** Snakemake builds each conda environment the first time a rule needs
it and downloads the packages then. Some clusters allow internet access on the
login node only. Which nodes have access is a property of your site (general
knowledge); ask your cluster's support if unsure.

**Fix.** Build all environments once, on a machine that has internet access
(for example the login node), before submitting the real run:

```bash
bash TTpipe.sh --conda-create-envs-only
```

This uses your config and profile and builds the environments without running
the analysis. Then submit as usual; the environments are reused. The
reference files and FASTQ files must of course already be on the cluster.

## Not covered here

Problems with logging in to a cluster (SSH keys, network or DNS errors) are
not TTpipe issues; your site's support is the place for those. If you hit
something that is not listed, open an issue with the failing rule's log, the
config you used and the output of `bash TTpipe.sh -n`.
